case.pattern_description: A shared-device fraud pattern was identified, affecting multiple customers' cards. A single handset profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) was used across 28 different cards in the same weeks, each time appearing as a new device for purchases ranging from $56.19 to $209.66. This pattern matched four confirmed closed cases, which the analysts could not attribute to any known fraud typology. The fraud was discovered by analyzing card -> transaction -> device relationships in TigerGraph.

sar.narrative: Customer C07472, holder of card C07472-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-11-30 15:47 and 2016-12-04 11:47, 2 transaction(s) totalling $265.85 were made on the card online from device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' through an anonymous proxy: $56.19 (3500431, 2016-11-30 15:47), $209.66 (3512563, 2016-12-04 11:47). The same device profile was used on 28 other customers' cards in the same period, most of them behind anonymous proxies and each time as a new device, indicating a common actor. The activity is suspicious because: Case-memory model score 0.325; Device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' was used by 28 cards in a 60-day window around the alert; 28 of them behind an anonymous/hidden proxy and 28 flagged as a New device. 4 closed case(s) on cards that used this profile were confirmed fraud, 4 of them recorded as an undocumented pattern. It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-2971. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placing linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
